title: Edge-current noise reversed two link-ranking methods in passive models of two partial adult worm maps
abstract: We tested whether a noise assumption changes electrical link recovery in two partial adult worm circuit models. With independent cell noise, inverse covariance had mean precision 0.9729 and 0.9685 at the known link count. One-lag regression gave 0.9425 and 0.9303. With conductance-matched noise, inverse covariance gave 0.0068 and 0.0096, while lag regression gave 0.9496 and 0.9337. Each setting used 12 exact stationary simulations of duration 1000 with step 0.05. Added edge-current noise at an intermediate strength also favored lag regression. At the matched limit, stationary covariance is exactly the identity, while the lag transition still contains wiring. This known linear-system mechanism supplies a controlled negative case for zero-lag inference. Partial maps, assumed conductance and noise, full voltage observation, no readout noise and an oracle link count limit the result. No measured activity was tested. Code, aggregate scores, source hashes, a figure and separate-data retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: Mean precision at the true link count changed with the noise model. Error bars give one standard deviation over 12 simulations per map. Duration is 1000 model units and step is 0.05. These are simulated voltages, not measured activity.
